LESSON: HANDWRITING

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: WRITING
Topic 4.3: Handwriting

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Handwriting. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should I write the learner should be able to: activities to practice letter patterns, word well?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use conventional spacing patterns, and sentence patterns between words  Learners observe and practice handwriting as
2. use basic punctuation is displayed appropriately  Learners engage in a variety of handwriting
3. join letters to form activities to improve their writing (capital and meaningful words small letters, commas and full stop), in groups
4. use capitalization pairs and individually appropriately  Learners participate in writing contests in

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: HANDWRITING
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Handwriting helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: HANDWRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use conventional spacing patterns, and sentence patterns between words  Learners observe and practice handwriting as

What this means
In this part you learn to use conventional spacing patterns, and sentence patterns between words  Learners observe and practice handwriting as. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use conventional spacing patterns, and sentence patterns between words  Learners observe and practice handwriting as.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Handwriting”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use conventional spacing patterns, and sentence patterns between words  Learners observe and practice handwriting as. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use basic punctuation is displayed appropriately  Learners engage in a variety of handwriting

What this means
In this part you learn to use basic punctuation is displayed appropriately  Learners engage in a variety of handwriting. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use basic punctuation is displayed appropriately  Learners engage in a variety of handwriting.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Handwriting to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use basic punctuation is displayed appropriately  Learners engage in a variety of handwriting. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Join letters to form activities to improve their writing (capital and meaningful words small letters, commas and full stop), in groups

What this means
In this part you learn to join letters to form activities to improve their writing (capital and meaningful words small letters, commas and full stop), in groups. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: join letters to form activities to improve their writing (capital and meaningful words small letters, commas and full stop), in groups.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can join letters to form activities to improve their writing (capital and meaningful words small letters, commas and full stop), in groups. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Use capitalization pairs and individually appropriately  Learners participate in writing contests in

What this means
In this part you learn to use capitalization pairs and individually appropriately  Learners participate in writing contests in. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use capitalization pairs and individually appropriately  Learners participate in writing contests in.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Handwriting”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use capitalization pairs and individually appropriately  Learners participate in writing contests in. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Handwriting is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Handwriting”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use conventional spacing patterns, and sentence patterns between words  Learners observe and practice handwriting as)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Handwriting to a partner. (skill: use basic punctuation is displayed appropriately  Learners engage in a variety of handwriting)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: join letters to form activities to improve their writing (capital and meaningful words small letters, commas and full stop), in groups)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Handwriting”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use capitalization pairs and individually appropriately  Learners participate in writing contests in)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Handwriting to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use conventional spacing patterns, and sentence patterns between words  Learners observe and practice handwriting as.
3. Practise this skill: use basic punctuation is displayed appropriately  Learners engage in a variety of handwriting.
4. Practise this skill: join letters to form activities to improve their writing (capital and meaningful words small letters, commas and full stop), in groups.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Handwriting from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Handwriting: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Handwriting?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should I write the learner should be able to: activities to practice letter patterns, word well?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Handwriting means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use conventional spacing patterns, and sentence patterns between words  Learners observe and practice handwriting as.
5. Be able to: use basic punctuation is displayed appropriately  Learners engage in a variety of handwriting.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
